elements.text: Welcome back class. Today we are examining Distributed Database Systems and Consensus Algorithms. First, let us establish what a distributed database actually is.

Notice the quorum requirement formula: majority = floor(n / 2) + 1. For a 5-node cluster, consensus requires at least 3 active nodes. In summary, Raft decomposes consensus into leader election, log replication, and safety constraints.

elements.meaning: a system of multiple interconnected databases stored across physically distinct computing nodes

elements.title: Welcome Back Class Points
items: First, let us establish what a distributed database actually is.
Second step: If an election timeout elapses without a heartbeat, the node becomes a Candidate.
Third step: The candidate requests votes from all peer nodes in the cluster.
Fourth step: If the candidate receives votes from a majority of nodes, it transitions to the Leader state.
Fifth step: The leader begins serving client writes and broadcasting append entries RPCs.

elements.text: important note: in any real-world distributed network, network partitions are inevitable, which means architects must choose between consistency and availability.
